quest.title: Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion
quest.description: By means of a special ceremony, you finally learn about the "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir's past.\nNow all that's left is to leave this place.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IV
chapter.title: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight

talks.objective: Return to the Curatorium of Secrets
Return to the Curatorium of Secrets

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Everyone, I'm back. Can I get a standing ovation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nefer! How are you holding up? Feeling okay?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Pff, she's fine! Boss is a pro.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You will have seen the events of Rerir's life through my thoughts. It's now clear that he is just a regular nobody driven by personal tragedy, as he said himself.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I mostly agree. There's only so much we can know about him from his memories alone, but they did give us a clear glimpse into his life in Khaenri'ah...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: However, I would not consider Rerir to be a "nobody." He was deeply involved in the events of that era. Yet, when the catastrophe of a generation strikes, nobody is safe.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sounds to me like you're speaking in riddles again. Is this you urging me not to abandon the people of Nod-Krai in their hour of need?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: That's not what I meant, although I do hope you choose to remain a part of the plan. Without you, the mission ahead will be all but impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Then try to remember that I respond better to the carrot than the stick. And I don't appreciate being bossed around.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now, as for you, missy... You were excellent. You stuck to the rules of the ceremony and kept your mouth shut the entire time. Bravo.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Cool — so can you fill me in on the deets now? Most of what I saw went right over my head...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Patience, you'll hear the whole story, don't you worry. But let's meet up with the others first — it will save me narrating it twice.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yes, Boss! Lemme get that door for ya...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's more like it. For a moment there, I was worried you'd forgotten about the first clause of your employment contract.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Forgive my curiosity, but... what does the first clause say...?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: It says I gotta do the annoying stuff that boss is too lazy to do for herself. Like, opening the door, pouring the tea, yadda-yadda.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Is that right...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...If something is in the contract, it's because she willingly agreed to it. Rest assured that the Curatorium abides by the very strictest of labor policies. You don't seriously think I'm cruel enough to treat her like my slave?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In any case, I've hardly shied away from my share of the work today. Hmph, hope I don't catch Flins and Varka lounging about in their chairs, enjoying a leisurely cup of tea...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: There's nothing I dislike more than other people enjoying themselves while I'm hard at work...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Sorry to disturb you, but we seem to have run into some trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Evidently so. Don't worry, I'm not about to leave you to fend for yourselves. I'm not that kind of boss, and it would go against the Curatorium's labor policy.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Um... I'm sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What did you hear me say? I wasn't talking about labor policy.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...How long have I been standing here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not long. You just appeared by the door a moment ago.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss, what's wrong? You look like you've seen a ghost...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We've been tricked. We never left at all... Somehow, I hallucinated that whole scene back inside the office.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hallucinated!? But how?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: How indeed... This place should heed my will alone. All thoughts and actions that occur in here are just a result of pawns moving across the chessboard in a carefully calculated manner. And nobody has access to this chess set but me...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So you control everything in here?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: More or less. But yes, it's a special technique of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has anything like this ever happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Only once. It was the first time I used the chess set.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Is there any similarity between what happened then and what's happening now?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm... I suppose my thoughts are a little turbulent, which was also the case my first time.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The first clause of your contract clearly states that I only need your help with things that I'm too lazy to do myself.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Meaning, you're not feeling lazy right now?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Meaning, this is not something Jahoda can help with. The chess set is a personal treasure that I alone understand. I must be the one to find our way out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss, it's fine, really! Let me do something useful!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Ah, listen to you... Whatever would I do without you, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: What? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes, really. Where would I ever find another employee as obedient and servile as you? God forbid anything ever happens to you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Uh, o—okay...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Well anyway, I was thinking of fetching some water. There's gotta be a source around here somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I suggest everyone finds someplace comfortable to take a rest. We gotta conserve our energy.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Even though all this chess malarkey doesn't exist in a physical sense, mentally speaking it's all real — and so is our tiredness and fatigue.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: You don't wanna dismiss mental fatigue! Just because it isn't physical doesn't mean it's any less serious. But anyway, I got your backs, so don't worry about a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Don't I have the best employees? Jealous much?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If we can find a suitable time, I'd love to borrow Jahoda for a day to help out at the Frostmoon Scions. Would you be amenable to that, Boss Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Oh, Lauma... Have I ever told you just how pretty you are? Beauty runs from the tips of your antlers... to the depths of your imagination.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Time to rally, everyone. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As we continue our journey, the same rules will apply. That means stay focused and no talking, no matter what we encounter. And don't disturb the chess pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You have my word that I will get us all out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Retenu
dialogues.text: Wasn't expecting visitors at this hour... Wait, is that...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Oh... it's him...)

dialogues.speaker: Retenu
dialogues.text: There you are! Sinuhe's been looking for you all day, I think he has some news for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? What were you doing just now, Uncle Retenu? Hiding away some more loose change? Hee-hee, I know I saw some Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Retenu
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "loose change"? Come on, I'm too old for this. Just pretend you saw nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Apepi
dialogues.text: Hey kid, mind telling me what Sinuhe's been up to recently? I'm trying to get in his good books and I need a way in!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: Get in his good books? Why? What do you want with my dad, Uncle Apepi?

dialogues.speaker: Apepi
dialogues.text: I've written a new song. I was hoping to showcase it at the next festival, but I'll need his approval.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: A new song, huh? I'd love to stay and listen, but unfortunately Uncle Retenu says my dad's looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Apepi
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well, there's plenty of time, and I'm not going anywhere. See that pile of stones? I'll be sitting there, warming up my vocal cords. Come find me when you're done.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: Pile of stones. Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: Hi, Dad! Uncle Retenu said you were looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: Ah, there's my little princess! If you'd gotten back just a little sooner, you could've shared the spoils of war with me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: Spoils of war? Who were you fighting against, Dad?

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: Hahaha, it was just a figure of speech. The aftermath of a sandstorm is no time to be waging war.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: I was talking about our war against thirst. I went out to fix our water supply problem — and now I'm back, which means...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: We have a well again!

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: That's right! I found a new one and brought back as much water as I could carry. It should last us for a good while.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: *sigh* If it wasn't for these blasted sandstorms, our wells wouldn't be caving in, and you wouldn't be spending all your time out searching for new water sources.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: As the chief of our tribe, I'm supposed to be leading us out of hardship and poverty, onto better things.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: You know how prosperous our ancestors were. I've told you all the stories... And look at us now, squeezed into these hovels. No one would choose this if it wasn't for the endless wars over the years.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: ...But things are looking up. I started working with some folks from the Akademiya a few months back. They gave me some contacts in return for my assistance in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: So you're the Akademiya's helper now?

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: Special ambassador, they call it. Think of it as a partnership.

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: It's nothing bad, okay? We've been isolated here in the desert for too long. Seeking opportunities elsewhere is the best thing for us, and the fastest way to progress.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer (Young)
dialogues.text: So... Do you get anything good out of being a special ambassador?

dialogues.speaker: Sinuhe
dialogues.text: Of course! My luck's improving all the time. One day, I swear I'm gonna lead us out of this place. We'll find somewhere new, somewhere better.

dialogues.speaker: Angry Uproar
dialogues.text: That's our well, and you know it! You stole from us! Hmph, well you've gone from chief to thief, and now you have to face the consequences!

dialogues.speaker: Angry Uproar
dialogues.text: Did you really think you could take our water without permission and get away with it? You're either brave, stupid, or both!

dialogues.speaker: Angry Uproar
dialogues.text: And that "special ambassador" act? Yeah, nice try! We spoke to the Akademiya. They said it was all news to them!

dialogues.speaker: Angry Uproar
dialogues.text: You're a liar and a cheat!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (I heard Jahoda gasp... But I don't blame her. Most people are terrified by the sight of blood.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Corpses strewn across the ground... The wounds are clearly from scimitars and daggers — the desert-dwellers' weapons of choice.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (There's a handwritten note on the ground. Let's see what it says.)

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: Haleel, this is Sinuhe, chief of the Shimti tribe. Surely, you remember me? I was the one who helped you and your colleagues avoid the quicksand in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: "This is my second time writing to you. I assume my last letter must have gotten lost in the mail, as I didn't receive a reply. I hope this one makes it to you safely."

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: I'm writing to you because I need some help. That sandstorm the other day completely blocked up our well, forcing me to look for another water source in Iab and Unut territory. It was a matter of survival.

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: Praise the gods — the well of the Iab tribe was intact. It was my last resort... I drew what water I could and left, but not without being spotted. I fear they will retaliate.

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: You told me to write to you if I ever needed help. You said you'd be my ally in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: I urgently need you to formally recognize my title of special ambassador and send some of your people to assist me for a few days. It's the only way I can convince them that this was the Akademiya's decision and prevent them from retaliating.

dialogues.speaker: A Handwritten Letter
dialogues.text: This is an emergency. Please send help as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Looks like this letter never got sent.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (The writer died a grisly death, and the letter was trampled into the ground. It's badly defaced — some parts are barely legible.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...What a ridiculous lie the surviving Shimti tell. Their whole village was butchered over a sip of water.)

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: Ah, officer! Welcome, welcome to our humble village...

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: I thought you would at least have the courtesy to provide some respectable libations.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: This is the finest wine Aaru Village has to offer, I promise...

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has agreed to reserve a single space for a candidate from your village. But I remain skeptical of this entire endeavor. I highly doubt anyone in this desert possesses serious academic potential.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: Please, have faith! If not in us, then in our god... The child we found shows great promise. I beg you, take her away from this place... Give her a chance. Don't let her talent go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: Hmm... I don't recognize her. New arrival?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: She showed up here a few days ago, and we took her in. She's a really bright kid. Please help... I'm begging you.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: So. Where are you from?
Nowhere special. Just a sand dune.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: What about the rest of your family? How many of you are there?
Just the one.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: It's only you?
Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: So no brothers, no sisters? No mother or father?
Any who have slept on a bed of sand, I call my brothers and my sisters. Apart from that, I have no family.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: Get over here. Sign your name on the form.

dialogues.speaker: Mahamata
dialogues.text: ...Nefer? Hm. You're rather fair-skinned for a desert-dweller.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Nefer, this term's assignments have been issued already. Please read through the materials thoroughly, conduct your own additional research, and then write an essay on the topic.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes, Professor. I'm aware. I just had a couple more questions I wanted to get your perspective on.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Oh? Please, ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well... I saw the other students' problem sheets, and I couldn't help but notice that my assignment is much easier than theirs. Do you really think I'm a weak student?

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: A weak student? Goodness, no — quite the opposite. You have a sharp mind... almost too sharp.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I think what you're saying is, a weak student wouldn't have noticed the discrepancy — and if they did, they certainly wouldn't complain about the lighter workload.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: You see? Sharp as they come. You see things the way they are, and I'm sure you know why they're like that...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Because of where I come from. Because I'm different.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: I'm sorry Nefer. I don't like it any more than you do, it's just...

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: ...Anyway. You said you had a couple of questions, what's the other one?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I wanted to check — if someone sent me a letter to the Akademiya, where do I go to collect it?

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Ah, your family wrote to you? Well, as long as they put your name on the envelope, someone should hand it right to you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Not exactly. It's not even a recent letter... I was just curious where the mail would end up if no one collects it.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: The House of Daena, I expect. I know there's a box for unclaimed mail somewhere in there — probably sitting on a shelf.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Whatever you're looking for, that'd be the place to start.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Okay, got it. Thank you, Professor.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Honestly, I... I feel like I've failed you. I'm supposed to be your teacher, but I haven't taught you anything.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hey, don't say that.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're a great teacher, and you do your best for all your students... But the rules are the rules. You're not allowed to teach students like me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's not just the Akademiya, either. The whole world bends over backwards for the successful, and leaves the losers to suffer and die.

dialogues.speaker: Manetho
dialogues.text: Oh, my dear child... Don't tell me you've given up on life already?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I haven't. I just think that if you want to make it in this world, you have to find a way to become successful.

talks.objective: Look for the box containing the letters

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This must be it. A big cardboard box full of unclaimed mail. And probably some letters that ended up here by mistake, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A dilapidations survey from Port Ormos... Looks like it's from a Corps of Thirty representative. What a strange thought... a bunch of mercs losing sleep over run-down buildings.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This one was never even opened. I guess the recipient didn't care what the Corps of Thirty had to say about anything.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Who was it addressed to...? Hmm, I don't recognize the name. But it must've been a Kshahrewar professor.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This one is addressed to the Amurta sage. The title is, "Changes Observed in Satyavada Life Symptoms"... Why do all these letters read like full-blown dissertations?

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: Ahem... "Guided by the incense, we became lost somewhere in the forest. All the barriers between levels of consciousness disappeared as our minds soared around in circles, looking for a branch to seek refuge on..."

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: In clinical terms, these symptoms fit the description of incense poisoning. The Amurta Darshan strictly prohibits the use of hallucinogenic substances, but I believe there are still people getting away with it.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: For example, my neighbor, who always breaks out into song and dance after using incense...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This seems like something the Akademiya would want to know about. Why wasn't it collected?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Wait... What's this written on the back? It's so small...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The note says: "The sender authored this letter while under the influence of mushrooms. I would send it back, but no return address was provided." Stamped by the Grand Conservator of the House of Daena.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This next one is addressed to... Grand Sage Azar?

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: A Few Words of Protest Regarding Recent Changes in Sumeru's Educational Policy

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: In recent years, the Akademiya has taken on a small number of students from the desert region, as per the policy to this effect.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: However, it appears to me that these students have not, in fact, been provided with educational opportunities that are, in any meaningful sense, equal to those enjoyed by their peers.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: As well as receiving dumbed-down assignments and perfunctory tutoring, they do not even have full access to the Akasha system!

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: Education is the fundamental purpose of this institution, which should go without saying in a nation whose founding virtues are knowledge and wisdom. I ask you, is the lip service we pay to the policy of education for desert students truly the standard of pedagogy to which the Akademiya aspires?

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: As Grand Sage, policy decisions are your prerogative. But do not forget your roots. You and I were once students too, as was everyone else in this institution.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: I do hope you will give some serious attention to this matter. I encourage you to discuss issues like this with myself and others, and listen to some alternative opinions.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Great letter. Shame it didn't get to where it needed to go.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And the sender is... Huh? Sage Cyrus of Spantamad?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Haha. I didn't realize anyone else even knew how bad students like me have it in this place.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So this is where letters from the sage of Spantamad end up? Nice one, Grand Sage. Really enlightened leadership.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Whatever — this isn't what I came here for. Moving on...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm not exactly holding out hope that a letter sent from the desert would even make it here. But if it did, where else would it end up if not in this box?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I can't believe how much discarded mail there is... Must have been years since someone last went through it all. And this is just one box — the whole House of Daena is boxes on shelves...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I don't believe for one second that any human being has sat down and read through all the documents in this place. Who has that much free time on their hands?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Wait! Could this be it?

dialogues.speaker: A Plain Letter
dialogues.text: Least fancy envelope in the box, written on crude-quality paper...

dialogues.speaker: A Plain Letter
dialogues.text: And of course it would be right at the bottom of the pile. Clearly, no one gave this letter so much as a first glance, let alone a second.

dialogues.speaker: A Plain Letter
dialogues.text: The handwriting on the envelope looks very familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: Greetings, Haleel. My name is Sinuhe, chief of the Shimti tribe. I was the one who came to you and your colleagues' aid when you ran into trouble in the Great Red Sand.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: I don't know how well you remember it now, but I brought you to safety and gave you some water and other supplies. You seemed very pleased, and told me your name.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: In my tribe, learning a person's true name is serious business, and I therefore see you all as friends. You were kind enough to leave your contact details so we could stay in touch.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: The Shimti tribe lives a harsh nomadic existence in the desert. You were sympathetic towards my plight, promising to make me a special ambassador of the Akademiya and help us find a way to make a better living.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: This brings me to my reason for writing. Our tribe has fallen on particularly hard times, and I would like to ask for your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: There was a terrible sandstorm a few days ago which blocked up the well in our land. To ensure my people's survival, I had no choice but to venture into Iab and Unut territory in search of an alternate water source.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: "The Iab and Unut are descended from the Thamudians, while we trace our ancestry to Tulaytullah. We worship the Lord of Flowers and have had relatively good relations with our fellow tribes up until now."

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: I found a well belonging to the Iab tribe. They declined to help us, but I really had no other option — so I took some water to keep me and my tribe alive. My actions are certain to incur their wrath.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: When we met, you assured me that you would be my ally in the Akademiya. I would like to take you up on that offer, because I really need your help. I wonder if you could send an Akademiya representative to meet with me?

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: That aside — the last time you were here, you mentioned that the Akademiya had started accepting students from the desert, and I told you a little about my daughter, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Contents
dialogues.text: We have next to no resources here in the desert, and my power and influence are limited. Would you consider enrolling my daughter at the Akademiya? She is a smart girl — I know she won't disappoint you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: From the outset, the Akademiya never took you seriously. Those things they promised were just empty words... I doubt they even remember the name "Sinuhe."

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And you were so emphatic that your luck had finally changed for the better...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...You swore you'd lead us to a better place one day. You spoke with such conviction, like you were the most powerful chief in the whole desert...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You liar... You lied about everything! You promised the world and delivered on none of it!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And who fell for it? Just me, by the looks of it. Despite your best efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Which makes you a pathetic liar. You weren't even any good at it...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I think I'll take over from here. Let me show you how it's done.

talks.objective: Take a look at the letters inside the box

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I just came to say goodbye. Thanks for everything you've done for me in my time here.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Nefer? You... You've packed your bags... Where are you going?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm quitting. Something's come up in my hometown. Gonna head back and deal with it.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: But this was a hard-won opportunity for you... You know that better than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It was. But it doesn't matter — I have more important things to deal with, and they can't wait.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh — and I didn't want to overfill my bags, so I left some incense on your desk.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What's wrong? I thought you liked incense? Although, I did read somewhere in the House of Daena that it has hallucinogenic effects... Don't use it all at once, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Isn't this the stuff you brought from your hometown? ...You're just letting me have it? But you said it's a rare and valuable commodity...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yeah, about that...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I lied. It's not rare at all. There's this bunch of ruins near my hometown that are practically overgrown with this plant.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's not worth much. Keep it, it's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: But, Nefer...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, that's all from me. You take care.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Don't forget me, okay? I mean... We're more than just classmates, right? We're friends!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yeah. I'll remember you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (I lied again. That incense is worth a fortune, and it's a rare find even in those ruins.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (And as for remembering her... I have far too much to do when I get back. No time to reminisce.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...I'll be lucky if I even make it through this alive. But either way, I expect I'll forget you pretty quickly.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Arif.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: So. What does the Akademiya want? Since they've sent their special ambassador, I assume there's a big business deal to be made? If not... I'd be very disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Please sir, lower your blade. You're lucky I'm the one they sent. Not all special ambassadors share my... admiration for the Iab people.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The ever-shifting balance of power in the desert reduced the once-great civilizations of this region to rubble and sand. But the story of the Iab has a very different trajectory. Others grew weak, but you grew strong, beginning in obscurity and moving to prosperity. You're the only ones who defied the trend.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: Huh. So you do know who you're dealing with.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This well is the perfect symbol of your strength, is it not? It used to belong to the Unut, but it looks like you have control over it now.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: You're not wrong. But I'm sure you didn't come all this way just to flatter us.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Of course not. I came to bring you some very good news — some information that recently came to light, which might just be your ticket to freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Records uncovered by the Vahumana Darshan show that a certain well currently under Iab control is built on top of some ancient ruins. These ruins are of great archaeological interest to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I checked the map carefully on my way over here, and I'm confident that this is the well in question. The Akademiya is offering fifty million Mora in return for excavation rights.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: F—Fifty million!?

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: No, wait.. If these ruins are as important as you say, fifty million's a little low, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Don't get greedy, Iab!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We know far more than you think. We know that you seized this well by force. Wasn't that the first step in your rise to power? To drive away the Unut and steal their water supply?

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: Tsk... So what if it was?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Don't worry. As unscrupulous as it was, it's something we're willing to overlook. The Akademiya is only interested in dealing with the de facto power holders in the region.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I hope I am making myself clear.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: And I hope your words are the truth. If I find out the Akademiya is trying to play me, I'll hunt down every one of your people and make you watch as I cut their heads off one by one...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hahaha... I assure you, Chief, that would not be in your long-term interests. You don't want to make an enemy of the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You see how I'm dressed, don't you? I appreciate that you've never been to the rainforest, but surely even you recognize an ambassador's attire when you see it?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And what does a barbarian like you have to lose anyway? Hahaha... You really think the Sumeru Akademiya would bother to come all this way just to lie to you? We have more important things to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: Alright, I take your point. The Akademiya is the highest authority in the land. I'm sure you're trustworthy people.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: In that case... hehe, we have a deal. We will sell you the excavation rights.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: I'd like to thank you, Ambassador. This is good news indeed — excellent news! In fact, it calls for a celebration! Would you do us the honor of staying a while and enjoying some Iab hospitality?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Gladly. I am partial to wine myself... and I trust you are as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So let's indulge in a few drinks together... in celebration of this momentous occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Elated, the Iab drink the night away. The prospect of their new wealth is almost as intoxicating as the wine.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But when the new day dawns, it brings some shocking news...

dialogues.speaker: Iab Tribesperson
dialogues.text: Chief! Chief, it's an emergency!

dialogues.speaker: Iab Tribesperson
dialogues.text: It's the Unut, they've... they've taken the well!

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: Well, don't just stand there! Take it back!

dialogues.speaker: Iab Tribesperson
dialogues.text: Yes, Chief!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I have every confidence in the Iab's military superiority. And yet...

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Unut's response was alarmingly fast. The day after we reach a deal, they seize the well? This can't be a coincidence... Perhaps there is a traitor in your midst.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: Uh... I—I don't think so...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I am obliged to remind you, Chief, that the Akademiya will only deal with the de facto power holders. If you cannot regain control over the well, I'm afraid you won't see a single Mora of that fifty million.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: No! Please, Ambassador, just give me some time. I swear, the Unut will not get away with this!

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: That well is ours, and so is the Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Glad to hear it. I will wait here for an update.

dialogues.speaker: Arif
dialogues.text: If there is a traitor... I will find them. In the meantime, make yourself at home. I'll report back as soon as I have an update.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe. Much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Wow. All it took was a few words, and I've got him wrapped around my finger... What an amazing feeling.)

dialogues.speaker: Nizar
dialogues.text: So in summary, Ambassador, the Akademiya would rather negotiate with our tribe instead of the Iab, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Iab are ruthless murderers who don't listen to reason. And now they have the gall to interfere in our research projects in the desert region.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So let me ask you, Chief. If you were the Akademiya, what would you do?

dialogues.speaker: Nizar
dialogues.text: Kill them all, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Precisely. The Akademiya does not tolerate those who stand in our way. The Iab have held back our academic pursuits for too long, and our patience is wearing thin.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: At the same time, there is simply no way that the Akademiya can be seen to be intervening in desert affairs. I'm sure you understand where I'm coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Nizar
dialogues.text: We have our own rules out here. If the rainforest-dwellers raised arms against a desert tribe, you'd start a bloody war.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Right. We can't confront them ourselves, but we can support their enemies. The Unut have always had strained relations with the Iab, which makes you our natural allies.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let me be clear: The Akademiya wishes to collaborate with the legally recognized rulers of the desert in this matter. We are asking for excavation rights to that well, and our offer is fifty million Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Nizar
dialogues.text: ...Say no more. I believe we have an understanding.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Good — then I suggest you get to work. Get us access to that well, and the Mora's yours.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (You see, dad? Lying is easy when you know how. People will believe anything.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ("Natural allies." Hah...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Weren't the Iab your allies once? You were quick to send them after us to protect your interests back when we "stole" that water... and now look at you. You're at each other's throats.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehehe... Hahahaha, ahahahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Look at yourselves! You may be vile, savage monsters, but your butchered bodies bleed like any others... You're no different. You're nothing special at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The monsters who destroyed my home... they're just ordinary, petty human beings. What a joke!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hahaha! I think we're even now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Maybe I've even done the desert a favor. It's a better place without all these people around.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, Sinuhe, my gullible fool of a father... Perhaps if you'd been as ruthless as I was today, our tribespeople would still be alive. In this dog-eat-dog world, a chief needs to be tough to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...But you couldn't do what had to be done. So I did it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Nefer, it's okay... All of this is in the past now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I believe I remember you promising to remain silent.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, but even so...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: (Jahoda, is there anything you can do to ease the tension?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You got this, Jahoda! It's your time to shine!)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Alright, time for a sharp turn onto a completely different topic!)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: So, um... anyway! That's enough of that. When are we getting out of this place?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Feels like we've been walking forever! I'm getting pretty tired. Lauma? You tired?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. If we can find somewhere to sit down, I could certainly do with a rest.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's not far now. There should be a temple just up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this situation about to reach a conclusion?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Really, a temple? That's where this story ends?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hmm... I guess that's how things go in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've been to a similar place with a friend from the desert before.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Desert-dwellers can never escape their destiny — or so everyone says. I never wanted to believe it, but looking back now... I'm as desert as they come.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You mentioned a temple. What's waiting for us there?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: My biggest trade secret of all.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah... Then I'm guessing it's where you got your power from. The power to peer into other people's minds.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Huh. I didn't know you were clued up on any other religions.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm no expert in the history of Sumeru, but since you come from the desert, I would imagine it has something to do with King Deshret.

choices.text: And the Seven Pillars who served him.
I have some friends with connections to this stuff.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ah, I know who you mean — General Mahamatra Cyno. The spirit of Hermanubis dwells within him.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: That's Boss Nef for ya! She knows everything!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Cyno's hardly a figure of obscurity. But I know about Sethos, too.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: What about him? Is he a big deal, or something?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, he's not a small deal, let's put it that way.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Please, this is the bare-bone basics. Save the flattery.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Thanks for your patience, everyone — I'm sure it's been a lot to take in. With any luck, that's our exit just up ahead.

choices.text: They are major figures in the desert belief system too.

talks.objective: Go to the entrance of the temple

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, uh-oh, uh-oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'm totally out of my depth here. I don't have anything to add about any of this stuff. Like, look at that statue, for instance.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I wanna do the whole name-dropping, this-girl-knows-her-stuff thing too, but... I've never seen anything like it before!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: A statue with the head of a bird...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like something out of King Deshret's mausoleum...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's Thoth, the Ibis King — one of the Seven Pillars of King Deshret. The legends say that he, the Crocodile King, and the Goat King were the three retainers of King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (This place looks familiar... That's not a good sign.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (There's someone up ahead. Time for a little chat.)
